clients.notes: Genesis agents client. Signs requests via vault-bound Ed25519 keypair (cato/vault_crypto.py, CATO_AP2_PUBKEY). Rotated a THIRD time on 2026-08-21 per Ben's decision (Option B in HANDOFF-CATO-GENESIS-XERO-DEMO-2026-08-21.md): Cato's local encrypted vault was reconstructed on 2026-08-20, generating this current CATO_AP2_PUBKEY, and every real GenesisTool.execute() call was failing 401 ap2_client_untrusted against the previously-trusted key (7G6FdR1XQVc1JlIo+o8xfJFIOi4UK/gq22YvXoy7des=, rotated in 2026-08-13, now DELETED/superseded below). IMPORTANT FLAG FOR NEXT SESSION: the new pubkey C0b5/ct/FoXrZ99mBj+LsDAPQGw3kBLFvl+ZlnvwDIg= is byte-for-byte IDENTICAL to the key that was explicitly DELETED (not disabled) during the 2026-08-13 rotation above, at that time described as belonging to an untested short-lived intermediate vault (2-4 credentials, missing GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN) whose private half was never confirmed to have completed a real accepted call and was not operator-controlled. This rotation restores trust in that exact key on the strength of the operator's current CATO_VAULT_PASSWORD successfully unlocking the live vault.enc and returning it via Vault.get('CATO_AP2_PUBKEY') on 2026-08-21 — i.e. the vault holding this key is the one currently controlled by the operator, which is the same standard used to justify the 2026-08-13 rotation the other direction. Next session should confirm via `cato vault list` / doctor whether this vault generation is complete (all expected credentials present) before treating this as fully resolved, and should NOT re-delete this key as untested without checking this note first. Previously-trusted key 7G6FdR1... is DELETED, not disabled, for the same reason: its private half lived only in the 2026-08-20-superseded vault generation and no operator controls it post-reconstruction. Vault.create()/unlock() still refuse to silently overwrite or auto-create an existing vault (see cato/vault.py and tests/test_vault_safety.py).
